country.comment: The review focuses on rural water supply in the United States (occasionally mentioning comparative loss percentages in Germany and France on PDF p. 13).
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF p. 2, Introduction

effect_estimate.comment: No meta-analysis or pooled statistical effect estimate is reported; the review provides a narrative thematic synthesis of 36 documents (note that Table 1 on PDF pp. 5-7 is rendered as an unextracted graphic in the PDF text, while Results and Discussion on PDF pp. 8-13 summarize the synthesis). Secondary descriptive figures cited from individual sources include rural US water supply access rising from 16% to 29% between 2000 and 2010 (PDF p. 9), 31% of state expenditure going to operational maintenance (PDF p. 10), and 11-14% US water distribution losses (PDF p. 13).
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported (narrative synthesis without meta-analysis; descriptively notes that at least 70% of the 36 included documents focused on rural water rights). Concludes that inadequate rural infrastructure, absent/fragmented rural regulatory bodies, unregistered connections, and low water rates hinder rural US water supply, and recommends reorganizing government structures to grant municipalities flexibility, partnering local governments with the Rural Community Assistance Partnership for regulatory oversight, adopting cost-recovery water pricing, and supporting community-based providers and federal conservation/self-supply programs (CSP and EQIP).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 8, Results and Discussion; PDF pp. 10-13, Discussion and Conclusion

mechanism_certainty.comment: Under CODEBOOK.md §9, systematic reviews (AMSTAR 2) cannot exceed 2. Here, certainty is 0 (inferred only) because the paper conducts a broad narrative synthesis and offers prescriptive policy recommendations without empirically observing administrative mechanisms in operation or documenting/testing a statistical or empirical descriptive association between specific legal/administrative variables and rural water access outcomes (note also Table 1 on PDF pp. 5-7 contains no extracted text).
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 8-13, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines rural water rights and municipal asset ownership (property), rural-urban classification and infrastructure/desalination planning (planning, service_area), water pricing, cost recovery, affordability, and federal subsidies/rebates (fees), municipal regulatory flexibility (discretion), community-based management and ownership (participation), multi-level governance gaps and coordination across federal, state, local, private, and RCAP actors (institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination), and technical/financial support agents and programs such as CSP, EQIP, and RCAP (bureaucratic_assistance).

sample_size.comment: Secondary systematic review sample: 65 documents initially identified on water management, 10 duplicates removed, 19 excluded at screening/eligibility, leaving 36 included documents (empirical and non-empirical sources from 1990 to 2019). Table 1 on PDF pp. 5-7 is an embedded graphic without extracted text, but exact counts are stated in Results on PDF p. 8.
sample_size.value: 36 included documents (out of 65 identified documents; 10 duplicates removed and 19 excluded; 1990–2019)

study_design.comment: Author-described PRISMA systematic review searching 7 electronic databases plus Google for US government reports (1990–2019), applying a 27-item checklist and 4-stage screening flowchart, followed by qualitative thematic synthesis without quantitative meta-analysis.
study_design.value: Systematic review following PRISMA guidelines with thematic narrative synthesis (1990–2019)
